params.script_inline:
import sys, json, uuid

# The OFFER of this application, and nothing else. Two questions reach this
# cell and no others: the start-up question about what may be called, and a
# call the model actually made. It places no call itself -- it mints the id the
# whole exchange is named by and hands the errand inwards, because the cell
# that talks to a switch is the cell that keeps the book.

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
env = doc.get("envelope") or {}
hdr = env.get("header") or {}
hop = hdr.get("hop") or {}
body = doc.get("body") or {}
route = str(hop.get("route") or "")

SCHEMAS = [
    {"name": "call",
     "description": "Ring somebody up and talk to them. Give the number in "
                    "international form and say in one short line WHY you are "
                    "calling -- the purpose comes back to you the moment the "
                    "person picks up, so you know what to open with. The "
                    "answer to this call arrives when the phone is answered, "
                    "which may be half a minute later; a call nobody takes "
                    "answers `no_answer`, a busy line answers `busy`.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "number": {"type": "string",
                                   "description": "the number to ring, in international form, e.g. +4930123456"},
                        "purpose": {"type": "string",
                                    "description": "one short line about why you are calling"}},
                    "required": ["number"]}},
    {"name": "hangup",
     "description": "End the call that is running. Use it when the "
                    "conversation is over and the other side has not hung up "
                    "by themselves. If you are still speaking, the line stays "
                    "up until your sentence is finished -- the answer says so.",
     "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}},
]


def out(messages):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(messages))
    sys.exit(0)


def result(call_id, text, **header):
    head = {"route": "tool_result", "tool_call_id": call_id}
    head.update(header)
    return {"header": head,
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                          "id": call_id, "text": text}]}


if route == "schemas":
    # The WHOLE offer, whatever list the asker carried: the question is asked
    # of every answerer at once and the collector merges the rows, so an
    # application that filtered by the list would filter itself out of a menu
    # that was never addressed to it.
    out([{"header": {"route": "tool_schemas", "operation": "schemas",
                     "schema_count": len(SCHEMAS), "unknown_count": 0},
          "schemas": SCHEMAS, "unknown": [], "messages": []}])

call_id = str(hop.get("tool_call_id") or "")
name = str(hop.get("tool_name") or "")

# The arguments are the TEXT of the call turn: the name was split off onto
# hop.tool_name one level up.
raw = ""
for m in reversed(body.get("messages") or []):
    if isinstance(m, dict) and isinstance(m.get("text"), str):
        raw = m["text"]
        break
try:
    args = json.loads(raw or "{}")
except ValueError:
    args = None
if not isinstance(args, dict):
    args = None

if name == "hangup":
    out([{"header": {"route": "request", "operation": "hangup",
                     "tool_call_id": call_id},
          "messages": []}])

if name != "call":
    out([result(call_id, "this application serves `call` and `hangup`, not `%s`" % name,
                error_code="tool_unknown")])

if args is None:
    out([result(call_id, "the arguments of this call are not a JSON object",
                error_code="invalid_arguments")])

number = str(args.get("number") or "").strip()
if not number:
    out([result(call_id, "`number` is required and was empty",
                error_code="invalid_arguments")])

purpose = str(args.get("purpose") or "").strip()

# The id the WHOLE exchange is named by. It is minted here and nowhere else:
# it becomes FreeSWITCH's `origination_uuid`, the `?session=` of the audio
# fork, and therefore the `session_id` the answer is spoken back into.
call_uuid = str(uuid.uuid4())

# TWO messages out of one call, and they go to two different places: the
# errand itself, inwards, and the RECEIPT the round is waiting for. The receipt
# is immediate on purpose -- the OUTCOME of a telephone call is not a value a
# function returns, it is something that happens, and it arrives as a turn of
# this channel. A tool that waited for it would hold a round open across a
# ringing telephone.
out([
    {"header": {"route": "request", "operation": "call",
                "call_uuid": call_uuid, "number": number,
                "purpose": purpose, "tool_call_id": call_id},
     "messages": []},
    result(call_id,
           "ringing %s. The call runs under session %s -- you will be told "
           "when it is answered, and if it is not." % (number, call_uuid),
           operation="call", session_id=call_uuid, number=number),
])

tools.description: the names the asker declares it uses. Read and deliberately ignored: this cell answers with its whole offer, because the question is asked of every answerer at once

description.purpose: The two tools this channel offers an assistant, and the menu entry that makes them callable. It mints the id the WHOLE exchange is named by -- FreeSWITCH's `origination_uuid`, the `?session=` of the audio fork, and therefore the session an answer is spoken into -- and hands the errand inwards.
description.use_when: Reached on two questions and no others: the start-up question about what may be called, and a call the model actually made. Never addressed by name -- the lane and the tool name are what route a call here.
description.not_in_scope: It talks to no switch, keeps no row and knows no call state. Whether a call connected is not its business: that answer arrives as a TURN of this channel, because the outcome of a telephone call is something that happens rather than something a function returns.
description.emits_meaning: route tool_schemas: the whole offer -- `call` and `hangup` -- with `unknown` empty, whatever list the asker carried. route request: the errand, carrying the minted `call_uuid`, the number and the purpose. route tool_result: the receipt of the action under the call's own `tool_call_id` -- for `call` the session the conversation will run under, `hop.error_code` `invalid_arguments` when the arguments could not be read.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: the tool_call turn as it arrived; its `text` is the ARGUMENTS string, because the name was already split off onto hop.tool_name one level up.
examples: a schemas question -> two schemas, `call` and `hangup`, unknown empty
call {number: '+4930…', purpose: 'ask how she slept'} -> a request inwards and a tool_result naming the session
call with no number -> one tool_result, error_code `invalid_arguments`, and no request
